transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Varela (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (MagnaHealth - Head of Infra), Tom Alvarez (MagnaHealth - CTO), Evelyn Moore (MagnaHealth - Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be noisy):
- POC scoping focused on private networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink), data residency (regions), and egress constraints for a healthcare customer.
- Discussed success criteria (latency/throughput targets, data isolation, SOC2/KMS), workload sizing, and benchmark plan.
- Agreed next steps: share network checklist, confirm regions/accounts, schedule 3-day benchmark in customer account / dedicated test infra.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate you making the time. quick intros, I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account. Marcus my solutions engineer is here.
[00:08] Priya: Hi, Priya here, head of infra at MagnaHealth. we, uh, run most stuff in AWS us-east-1 and us-west-2, and security is obviously a big part.
[00:13] Tom: Tom, CTO. We'll be tied in for perf and cost decisions.
[00:16] Evelyn: Evelyn, security lead. I'll be driving SOC2 and KMS conversations.
[00:20] Marcus: Great, thanks. The aim today is to nail down the POC scope around private networking and data residency — VPC peering vs PrivateLink, exact regions, any egress restrictions, and success criteria for the pilot.
[00:31] Priya: Yeah we want to keep all inference traffic inside our accounts, ideally. No traffic to open internet, we want private endpoints.
[00:36] Lena: Totally — that matches the use cases we've done for other healthcare orgs. Marcus, do you want to walk high level on connectivity options?
[00:43] Marcus: Sure. So, Redwood supports a couple patterns: VPC peering into a dedicated Redwood VPC, AWS PrivateLink endpoints for model endpoints, or running Redwood Private in a customer VPC / on-prem if you need full control. For a POC most customers choose either VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on routing and cross-account restrictions.
[01:02] Marcus: VPC peering is straightforward if you can accept route table updates and don't need transitive routing. PrivateLink is better when you want endpoint-based access without touching route tables, but it requires us to manage NLBs and interface endpoints on your side. Both can be constrained to specific regions.
[01:17] Priya: Hmm, our security team prefers PrivateLink because we don't want to open peering across accounts — it's easier for auditing. But we need to confirm egress behavior, like will there be any calls to outside AWS or third-party telemetry?
[01:29] Marcus: Good question. By default, Redwood's inference path is contained within the configured VPC and region when you use PrivateLink or dedicated deployment. We do not route user payloads to third-party services. There is optional telemetry for metrics — that can be routed to your account endpoints or disabled during the POC.
[01:46] Evelyn: And encryption? KMS? We require customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest, and we need to see audit logs for model access.
[01:54] Marcus: We support KMS integration for private deployments and can integrate with your CMK for logs and storage. For hosted/dedicated POC we can enable encryption and provide access logs; we'll need to coordinate IAM roles and service principals.
[02:07] Tom: On workload — we run about 10k inference requests per day currently for our triage pipeline, avg prompt length about 150 tokens, but during peak loads it can hit 50 RPS for short bursts. We need p95 latency under 600ms for a 512-token max seq in the POC.
[02:23] Marcus: That's helpful. For sizing, we typically recommend a small dedicated pool for that profile, for example 1-2 GPU nodes depending on model choice and quantization. For benchmarking we usually stress both single-node latency and autoscaling behavior.
[02:36] Priya: Can you give more detail on the benchmark plan? We want something reproducible in our accounts.
[02:40] Marcus: Absolutely. Proposal: 3-day benchmark window. Day 1 stability and cold-start behavior, Day 2 steady-state throughput at your expected average (10k/day), Day 3 a stress run to simulate 2x peak (100 RPS) for short windows to validate autoscaling / throttling. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, errors, token/sec, and per-request logs for sampling. We'll also produce a cost projection comparing hosted vs dedicated for your traffic profile.
[03:04] Lena: We'll share a JMeter/locust profile and a sample dataset — you can run it from your account against PrivateLink endpoints or we'll run it on our test infra if you prefer.
[03:14] Priya: We'd like to run it in our account so networking is realistic. Also need to know egress IP ranges in case our outbound rules have to allow something.
[03:22] Marcus: For PrivateLink, traffic stays in your VPC; there's no public egress for inference payloads. We will, however, need to whitelist the interface endpoint service name during setup and potentially the NLB health check ranges. We'll provide the exact NLB CIDR ranges. For any optional telemetry to Redwood systems we can either route that through your logging endpoints or disable it for POC.
[03:41] Evelyn: Okay that's good. Also need to confirm region residency — primary storage and inference must be in us-east-1, no replicas to other regions without explicit permission.
[03:50] Marcus: We can pin the model endpoints and storage to us-east-1. If you later want multi-region failover we can discuss secondary regions but for the POC we'll keep it single-region.
[03:58] Tom: On success criteria: 1) p95 < 600ms for 512 tokens under steady-state, 2) error rate < 0.5%, 3) data remains in our account/region, 4) KMS-managed encryption and audit logs available, 5) cost projection within our target — about $X per 1k requests (we'll share exact target offline).
[04:18] Lena: Nice and clear. We'll encode those as the POC acceptance criteria. Marcus, any special notes about model variants/quantization we should call out?
[04:25] Marcus: Yeah, depending on model size we can run quantized variants (4-bit, int8-like profiles) to get better throughput. For a fidelity-first POC we should test both full-precision baseline and a recommended quantized profile, measure latency and quality. We'll log generation deltas so you can sanity check for regressions.
[04:41] Priya: For the benchmark dataset, some prompts include PHI-like context. Is Redwood willing to sign a narrow DPA for the POC and keep payloads restricted?
[04:50] Lena: We can provide a POC DPA and NDA. For payloads containing PHI, we strongly recommend masking or anonymizing for the initial test. If you need to send real PHI, we'll route everything through your private deployment with your KMS and ensure contractual controls; we'll need legal to review.
[05:05] Evelyn: We'll probably anonymize for the stress tests. For auditability we need request logging with identifiers but not full PHI content in Redwood-managed logs.
[05:12] Marcus: We can sample logs and redact content in-flight; we'll show you the log format and redaction options.
[05:19] Tom: Timeline — if we get the network checklist this week, can Redwood stand up the POC infra in our account early next week? We have a change freeze on 11/30 so need to wrap network changes before then.
[05:30] Marcus: If we get the accounts and endpoint role details by 11/23, we can provision the interface endpoints and NLBs by 11/25 and start the benchmark 11/27. That would give you time to review results before freeze.
[05:41] Priya: 11/23 is tight but doable. We'll confirm the AWS accounts and ownership contacts today.
[05:45] Lena: Great. On the POC scope length — are we aligned to a 2-4 week POC?
[05:50] Tom: 3 weeks should be enough for benchmarking and a quality sign-off.
[05:53] Marcus: Perfect, proposed plan: provision week of 11/25, run benchmarks 11/27-11/29, produce report by 12/2, review with you 12/3, then decide on expansion.
[06:05] Priya: One more item — network egress billing. We need to confirm whether there are any unexpected egress costs from Redwood-managed infra.
[06:11] Marcus: For PrivateLink, the data path is inside AWS and you pay interface endpoint charges and any NAT egress if you route traffic out. There shouldn't be extraneous egress to Internet. If we host dedicated infra in our account or yours, egress is standard AWS billing. We'll provide an estimated cost table.
[06:26] Evelyn: We'll need proof of SOC2-type controls, do you have a whitepaper or attestation we can review?
[06:31] Lena: Yes, we'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 summary. For POC we can give a redacted report; full report available under an NDA.
[06:40] Tom: Any blockers for model selection? We may want a smaller Llama-style open model, nothing huge for the POC.
[06:46] Marcus: We can run an LLM-7B variant quantized for latency, and also test a 13B as a quality comparison — both are supported. We will provide a quality eval run as part of the benchmark.
[06:56] Priya: Ok. On the networking checklist, can you include steps for VPC endpoint creation, route table updates if peering, SG settings, and sample Terraform?
[07:05] Marcus: Yup, sample Terraform, AWS CLI snippets, and a checklist of required IAM permissions — we'll include.
[07:11] Lena: Let's recap decisions and next steps. Decisions: PrivateLink preferred for this POC, single-region us-east-1 residency, anonymized PHI for tests, benchmark plan is 3 days with specific perf targets.
[07:25] Lena: Next steps: Redwood sends the network checklist, security docs, pricing estimate and the load test scripts. MagnaHealth to confirm AWS accounts, whitelist requirements, and SOC2 contact.
[07:36] Tom: Sounds good. One small question — any concerns about IP allowlist rotation during the POC window? We usually rotate keys weekly.
[07:42] Marcus: We can support short rotation windows; we'll coordinate a maintenance window for any endpoint updates. PrivateLink helps reduce rotation surface since it uses interface endpoints in your account.
[07:53] Priya: ok. if you can send the checklist today i'll get the team to start the work.
[07:57] Lena: Will do. We'll aim to send the package (network checklist, SOC2 summary, sample Terraform, pricing) by end of day 11/21.
[08:04] Evelyn: last ask — can you include a sample audit log entry schema so we can map to our SIEM?
[08:10] Marcus: Yes, we'll include log schema and redaction options.
[08:15] Lena: Perfect. Anyone else?
[08:18] Tom: nope, thanks everyone.
[08:20] Priya: thanks.
[08:22] Lena: Great, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and owners.

Meeting end.
